india.label: Cyclone · 17 Nov, 2:30 a.m. IST
india.headline: Akvan forms as Andhra and south Odisha go on orange alert
india.summary: Akvan became a cyclone on 16 November. The IMD’s early Tuesday bulletin forecast that it could cross the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Nellore and Tuni around midday on 20 November as a very severe cyclone.
india.context: Fishing and coastal transport could be disrupted. Check the latest IMD track and district advisories as the forecast evolves.
india.why: IMD raised the alert after the Bay of Bengal system strengthened into a cyclone.

india.label: Wholesale prices · 16 Nov
india.headline: India’s wholesale inflation rises to 12.29%
india.summary: October wholesale prices rose 12.29% year on year, up from 11.39% in September. Fuel and power prices rose 32.84%, while manufactured-products inflation eased to 9.54%.
india.context: Watch whether softer crude reduces costs for energy-intensive businesses and whether price increases reach consumers.
india.why: A jump in fuel and power inflation outweighed slower price increases in manufactured products.

india.label: Population count · 16 Nov
india.headline: Census 2027 opens online population counting in four states
india.summary: Optional online self-enumeration opened on Monday in Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. Residents can submit population details online through 30 November.
india.context: Door-to-door enumeration in those areas runs from 1 December to 4 January. Check the official census portal for the instructions for your area.
india.why: The Census is opening online self-enumeration ahead of door-to-door visits in these areas.

india.label: Bank capital · 16 Nov
india.headline: RBI seeks review of the Yes Bank bond write-off ruling
india.summary: Reuters reported on Monday that the RBI had petitioned the Supreme Court to review its decision setting aside the ₹8,415 crore write-off of Yes Bank’s additional Tier 1 bonds.
india.context: AT1 bonds can absorb losses when a bank is in distress. Watch whether the court takes up the review and clarifies when a write-off can be ordered.
india.why: The court set aside the loss-absorbing bond write-off, prompting the RBI to seek a review.

india.label: Jobs · 16 Nov
india.headline: India’s unemployment rate edges down to 4.9%
india.summary: The official survey for people aged 15 and above showed unemployment at 4.9% in October, down from 5.0% in September. Urban unemployment fell to 6.7%, and rural unemployment held at 4.2%.
india.context: The share of women aged 15 and above who were working rose from 32.8% to 33.3%. Watch whether the gain continues alongside rising participation.
india.source: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
india.why: The survey recorded a drop in urban unemployment while rural unemployment held steady. The release does not establish what caused those changes.

sources.label: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

world.label: Ukraine · 17 Nov
world.headline: Kyiv reports water and power cuts after bridge strikes
world.summary: Kyiv’s mayor said preliminary reports pointed to Russian strikes on two Dnipro bridges and other infrastructure late on 16 November local time. He reported water and power cuts in parts of the capital.
world.context: Watch restoration updates and bridge access. Prolonged outages could disrupt transport and heating as winter approaches.
world.why: Kyiv’s mayor linked the outages to strikes on bridges and other infrastructure. The initial damage reports were preliminary.

world.label: Sanctions · 16 Nov
world.headline: EU sanctions 113 Russia-linked people and entities
world.summary: The EU added 12 people and 101 entities to its sanctions list on Monday. They include nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, as well as targets linked to the oil trade and shadow fleet.
world.context: Banks, insurers and shipping companies face new checks on counterparties. Watch the published list and how financial institutions apply the restrictions.
world.why: The EU says it is targeting banking and oil-trade networks to limit Russia’s ability to finance the war.

world.label: Iran energy · 16 Nov
world.headline: Iran braces for deeper winter gas shortages after war damage
world.summary: Iran faces a projected worsening of winter gas shortages. Reuters reported that most regions could be affected.
world.context: Prolonged shortages could strain home heating and gas-dependent factories. Watch repair schedules and rationing notices.
world.why: Iran’s gas company attributes the expected shortfall to damage at four processing plants.

world.label: Diplomacy · 16 Nov
world.headline: China confirms 19 November summit with Trump and Putin
world.summary: Beijing confirmed that Xi Jinping will meet Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC. Trump said he plans to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine.
world.context: Watch for a joint statement or a commitment to follow-up talks. The confirmed meeting gives the three governments a channel for direct talks on security.
world.source: China Ministry of Foreign Affairs · Meeting announcement
world.why: Beijing confirmed the meeting on the sidelines of APEC. Trump said he wants to discuss the war in Ukraine.

sources.label: China Ministry of Foreign Affairs · Meeting announcement

world.label: Climate finance · 17 Nov
world.headline: Nepal presses for flood recovery funding at COP31
world.summary: Nepal called for more support for flood-hit communities at the UN climate summit in Türkiye. AP reported that the loss-and-damage fund pledged about $20 million for Nepal, against estimated losses of $2.5 billion.
world.context: The next test is how soon the pledge reaches people and whether further funding covers homes, roads and damaged hydropower facilities.
world.why: The pledged funding covers only a fraction of the estimated losses from floods.

markets.label: Opening trade · 17 Nov, 9:42 a.m. IST
markets.headline: Nifty and Sensex edge higher as cheaper oil lifts sectors
markets.summary: At 9:42 a.m. IST, Nifty 50 and Sensex were each up 0.19%, at 25,338.70 and 82,261.31. The Tuesday cash session opened flat after Monday’s gains. Twelve of 16 major sectors rose.
markets.context: Reuters linked cheaper crude to gains in fuel retailers (around 1%), tyre makers (up to 4%) and paint stocks (1.4–2.5%). Watch whether these gains hold as oil moves.
markets.why: Reuters linked the gains to cheaper oil, which can help fuel retailers’ margins and lower costs for tyre and paint makers.

markets.label: Commodities · 17 Nov a.m.
markets.headline: Brent slips to $91.70 and Indian bullion gold is ₹1,34,971
markets.summary: Brent reached $91.70 a barrel on Tuesday morning. IBJA’s 16 November evening benchmark for 999 gold was ₹1,34,971 per 10 grams.
markets.context: Senco reported festive retail sales up 26% year on year. Shares rose 4.7% in early trade. Watch jewellery margins and crude import costs.
markets.why: Reuters attributed the fall in Brent to recovering Gulf exports and expectations of surplus supply.

sources.label: Reuters · Brent and early share moves

markets.label: Foreign exchange · 17 Nov, 9:02 a.m. IST
markets.headline: Rupee strengthens to ₹93.73 at Tuesday’s open
markets.summary: Moneycontrol reported an opening ₹93.73 per US dollar. Reuters put Monday’s close at ₹93.9225 and November’s foreign equity inflows at $9.53 billion.
markets.context: Importers can monitor whether the rupee holds its gain as crude and US yields move.
markets.why: Moneycontrol cited cheaper crude and renewed foreign equity inflows as support for the rupee.

markets.label: Exchange filing · 16 Nov evening
markets.headline: US approval opens BSE BANKEX futures to US-based investors
markets.summary: BSE said the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved offering its BANKEX index futures to US-based investors, under applicable rules. BANKEX tracks Indian banking stocks.
markets.context: A wider pool of participants could increase liquidity. Watch trading volumes and spreads once overseas access is available.
markets.why: The US regulator approved access to a contract that tracks Indian banking stocks.

markets.label: Primary market · 17 Nov morning
markets.headline: Crystal Crop schedules anchor bids before its public IPO
markets.summary: Crystal Crop Protection’s prospectus schedules anchor bidding for 17 November. Public bidding runs 18–20 November at ₹259–272. Mahanadi Coalfields and SME issuer Watrana Rentals are due to open on 19 November.
markets.context: Anchor bidding precedes the public window. Upstox’s calendar showed no IPO listings this week. Check exchange notices for timetable changes.
markets.why: The anchor round comes before the public window under the timetable in the prospectus.

sources.label: Upstox · Weekly IPO and listing calendar

investing.label: NSE: PETRONET · 16 Nov close
investing.headline: Petronet LNG’s terminal economics depend on utilisation
investing.summary: Dahej processed 216 trillion BTU in Q2 FY27, up from 211 a year earlier. Petronet reported ₹1,235 crore in quarterly profit after tax.
investing.why: Dahej and Kochi provide established import and regasification capacity. Terminal infrastructure and customer contracts are costly to replicate.
investing.valuation: ₹326 on 16 November NSE close. About 10.6× trailing earnings, modestly below the 11.0× one-year median reported in the valuation snapshot.
investing.context: The value case improves if higher Dahej throughput persists and new capacity adds cash flow. Watch volumes, utilisation and capex returns.
investing.risk: A small valuation discount provides limited protection if LNG costs curb demand or new projects dilute returns.

sources.label: HV Investing · Trailing valuation and median
HDFC Securities · Capex and margin analysis

investing.label: NSE: POWERGRID · 16 Nov close
investing.headline: Power Grid’s growth case rests on commissioning
investing.summary: Q2 consolidated profit rose 8% to ₹3,866 crore. It capitalised ₹9,300 crore of assets in the first half of FY27.
investing.why: Its national transmission network is hard to replicate. Regulated assets can provide predictable returns, while new projects still face bidding competition.
investing.valuation: ₹262.20 on 16 November NSE close, about 15.1× trailing earnings. If annual EPS reaches ₹19, that same price is 13.8× earnings.
investing.context: An expanding grid can bring more projects into the earning asset base. Watch the gap between capex and commissioning.
investing.risk: Delays, weaker bidding returns and higher financing costs can erode the growth case.

investing.label: NSE: COALINDIA · 16 Nov close
investing.headline: Coal India is cheap on earnings if those earnings hold
investing.summary: Q2 profit attributable to shareholders rose about 53% to ₹6,516 crore. The company declared a ₹10.25 interim dividend.
investing.why: Scale, mine access and established supply relationships give India’s largest coal producer an advantage.
investing.valuation: ₹397.50 on 16 November NSE close, about 7.3× trailing EPS of ₹54.14, near its 7.4× five-year median. At ₹45 EPS it would be 8.8×.
investing.context: Watch dispatches and auction prices to see if earnings hold. The Mahanadi IPO is a potential unlock through a share sale, separate from operating growth.
investing.risk: Lower realisations, rising costs and slower coal demand could make current earnings and the dividend hard to sustain.

sources.label: Fin Cascade · Earnings and valuation history

investing.label: NSE: IEX · 16 Nov close
investing.headline: IEX’s valuation depends on what changes under market coupling
investing.summary: Q2 FY27 electricity trading volumes rose 12.7% to 39.7 billion units. Consolidated net profit grew 12.9% to ₹139.24 crore.
investing.why: A large buyer and seller network helps draw orders to its platform. Common clearing prices could weaken that advantage.
investing.valuation: ₹115.54 on 16 November NSE close. If annual earnings settle at ₹6 per share it is 19.3× earnings. At ₹5 it is 23.1×.
investing.context: Growth in exchange-traded power makes the idea interesting if volumes and fees hold. Watch final CERC rules and order flow after implementation.
investing.risk: Market coupling could shift volumes to rivals or pressure fees. The earnings scenarios are sensitivity checks.
investing.source: NSE · IEX earnings call and coupling discussion

sources.label: NSE · IEX earnings call and coupling discussion

investing.label: NSE: CAMS · 16 Nov close
investing.headline: CAMS has a strong moat and a demanding price
investing.summary: CAMS reported 67% mutual-fund assets serviced and Q2 FY27 profit growth of 14.4%. Non-mutual-fund revenue grew 21.7%.
investing.why: Fund houses rely on CAMS for transaction processing and recordkeeping. Scale and integration can make switching costly.
investing.valuation: ₹723.30 on 16 November NSE close, about 34.6× annualised H1 EPS of ₹20.92. A 28× multiple at this price would require ₹25.83 annual EPS.
investing.context: The growth case depends on sustained mutual fund flows and profitable expansion outside fund servicing. Track non-fund contribution and margins.
investing.risk: The premium leaves little cushion for slower flows, fee pressure or a drop in market share.
investing.source: NSE · CAMS Q2 earnings and market share

sources.label: NSE · CAMS Q2 earnings and market share

tech.label: AI export controls · 16 Nov
tech.headline: US tightens rules on remote access to advanced AI chips
tech.summary: The US Commerce Department issued an interim final rule covering remote access to certain advanced American AI chips and servers.
tech.context: Cloud providers serving restricted destinations may need to review contracts and licensing. Watch their implementation notices.
tech.source: US Bureau of Industry and Security
tech.why: US officials say the restrictions address access routed through data centres in third countries.

sources.label: US Bureau of Industry and Security

tech.label: AI supply chains · 16 Nov
tech.headline: India joins US-led pact to secure AI supply chains
tech.summary: The United States, India and eight other countries signed the San Francisco Declaration to protect sensitive technology and AI infrastructure. Working groups are planned for policy, adoption, supply chains and security.
tech.context: Watch which groups turn cooperation into projects or standards. Semiconductor and critical-mineral suppliers could see new cross-border opportunities.
tech.why: The signatories identified fragile technology supply chains as a shared economic and security risk.

tech.label: AI models · 16 Nov
tech.headline: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max with a million-token context
tech.summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max through QwenCloud and its own apps. It says the model can take a million tokens of context and process visual input.
tech.context: Long context can help teams work with larger document sets. Test retrieval quality, latency and cost on your own documents before moving a workflow.
tech.why: Alibaba says the release is designed to handle visual input and much longer documents in one request.

tech.label: AI training · 17 Nov
tech.headline: Chinese AI developers scale up training from US models
tech.summary: A Reuters review of more than 300 documents found Chinese developers are using answers and code from US AI systems to train smaller models. The technique, called distillation, can transfer selected skills at lower running cost.
tech.context: Watch how AI providers enforce terms on training rivals, and whether smaller models prove reliable enough for factories.
tech.why: Training smaller models on answers from larger systems can preserve selected skills at lower running cost.

tech.label: Quantum computing · 16 Nov
tech.headline: IBM, Fermilab and Nvidia plan a hybrid quantum testbed
tech.summary: The partners announced plans to combine IBM quantum processors with Nvidia’s accelerated computers. Researchers will use the platform to study modular designs and try methods for correcting quantum errors.
tech.context: Watch for results on real hardware, especially whether error correction and networking hold up as more processors are connected.
tech.why: The partners want to test how classical accelerated computers can support modular quantum hardware and error correction.

mind.label: Human behaviour · 2026
mind.headline: Decision cues help AI simulations reproduce group behaviour
mind.summary: Researchers analysed 231 sessions of the Beer Distribution Game, where players’ orders can amplify demand swings. Giving language-model agents descriptions of how people decide brought seven models’ group behaviour closer to the human data.
mind.context: Compare a simulation with actual decisions before using it to set policies. This result comes from a specific supply-chain game.
mind.why: The cues gave models information about how people actually decide in the game.

mind.label: Memory · 2015
mind.headline: A claim can sound truer the second time you hear it
mind.summary: In experiments by Fazio and colleagues, participants rated repeated statements as truer than new ones. The effect appeared even for some false statements whose answers participants knew.
mind.context: When a claim feels familiar, ask what evidence supports it and where you saw it first. Familiarity can make a statement easier to accept.
mind.why: The researchers proposed that repetition makes a claim easier to process, which can feel like evidence that it is true.

mind.label: Judgment · 1994
mind.headline: Past projects can make your next deadline estimate better
mind.summary: Experiments on the planning fallacy found that people underestimated their own task completion times. In one study, explicitly connecting forecasts to relevant past experiences removed the optimistic bias.
mind.context: Before estimating a deadline, look up how long comparable tasks took. Then adjust for measurable differences such as staffing or scope.
mind.why: People tended to focus on the plan they imagined and gave too little weight to how long past tasks had taken.

mind.label: Human evolution · 2022
mind.headline: Milk use predates widespread lactose digestion in adults
mind.summary: Ancient pottery residues and DNA indicate that Europeans used milk for millennia before the variant for continued lactase production in adulthood became common. Researchers found support for famine and infection as possible selection pressures.
mind.context: A cultural practice can spread before a genetic change. The proposed roles of famine and disease came from historical proxies, so the mechanism remains a hypothesis.
mind.why: The researchers proposed that famine and infection could have made lactose digestion more consequential for survival.

mind.label: Evolution · 2021
mind.headline: Invasive cane toads evolved both attack and defence tactics
mind.summary: Australian cane toad tadpoles ate more hatchlings than tadpoles from the native range. In experiments, invasive hatchlings developed faster in response to cannibal cues.
mind.context: Competition within a species can shape traits on both sides of the interaction.
mind.why: Intense cannibalism can favour hatchlings that move through the vulnerable stage sooner.

marketing.label: India · Sunfeast · 16 Nov
marketing.headline: Sunfeast turns a Chhath greeting into a shared Patna tribute
marketing.summary: Sunfeast Mom’s Magic invited families to make WhatsApp keepsakes from Chhath memories, using a Madhubani motif by artist Dulari Devi. The brand planned to combine uploaded photos in a sun-shaped installation near Patna’s Gandhi Ghat.
marketing.context: Give people something personal to share. A local artist and a public installation can connect that action to a ritual the audience already values.
marketing.why: The campaign tied a family ritual to WhatsApp sharing and used local art to connect the digital keepsakes with Patna.

marketing.label: India · Gap · 13 Nov
marketing.headline: Gap puts an illustrator’s work on 3D mall screens
marketing.summary: Gap India used perspective, motion and scale on large mall screens in Mumbai and Noida to showcase its Fall 2026 clothing collaboration with illustrator Yash Pradhan.
marketing.context: Put product discovery close to where people can shop. Design the animation around the screen’s viewing angle and the few seconds passers-by will give it.
marketing.why: The mall screens put the artwork in front of shoppers near the point of purchase.

marketing.label: India · Spinz · 12 Nov
marketing.headline: Spinz makes 15 minutes the hook for a skincare ad
marketing.summary: CavinKare promoted the Spinz face pack with a 15-minute routine, using TV in North and West India and social platforms including YouTube.
marketing.context: A specific, substantiated time claim gives viewers a practical way to judge a routine.
marketing.why: A specific time cue helps viewers picture how the product might fit into their routine.

marketing.label: Global · Meow Mix · 16 Nov
marketing.headline: Meow Mix rewrites the origin stories of viral cats
marketing.summary: US cat-food brand Meow Mix gave Keyboard Cat, Table Cat and Huh Cat fictional backstories in three 30-second films. It rewrote its jingle for the spots and extended the campaign through TikTok, other social channels and creator partnerships.
marketing.context: Recognisable characters give a short ad a head start. Adapt the story to the channels where people already share the joke.
marketing.why: Familiar characters give people a reason to notice a short ad before they know the story.

marketing.label: Global · Netflix · 10 Nov
marketing.headline: Netflix sells the surprise of finding an unexpected favourite
marketing.summary: Netflix launched three 35mm films in the US, Canada, Brazil and Spain about the surprise of becoming a fan. Its US-only Typecast social series featured creators revealing their actual Netflix favourites.
marketing.context: Give a service benefit a human reaction people recognise. A short social series can turn the same idea into an invitation to share.
marketing.why: The films made an abstract benefit visible through the surprise of finding a favourite.
